item.title: Ban on appointing ILA chief: Smotrich slams High Court, calls ruling a 'legal injustice'
item.description: Smotrich slammed the High Court for delaying Yehuda Eliyahu’s appointment as Israel Land Authority director-general until after the elections, vowing to remove 'extremist elements' from the judicial system.

item.title: Join the Livestream: Torah MiTzion turns 30
item.description: The leading Torah-Zionist mission movement, which has established dozens of Batei Midrash and Kollels worldwide, will mark 30 years of activity with a festive tribute evening. The event will bring together hundreds of emissaries (shlichim), alumni, and community leaders from Israel and abroad.

item.title: During visit to Seam Line, Netanyahu warns terrorists: 'Don't test us'
item.description: The Prime Minister visited the seam line in Samaria alongside senior security officials and declared that the IDF is prepared for a scenario in which PA security forces turn their weapons against Israel.

item.title: Trump on if he'll endorse candidate in Israel: 'Maybe I'll do something'
item.description: US President Donald Trump responded to the question of whether he would recommend a candidate in the Israeli elections: "Maybe we'll do something."

item.title: Former hostage: 'I am still recovering'
item.description: Former hostage Segev Kalfon marks one year since release, reflects on 738 days in captivity: 'Still learning to live again.'

item.title: Three hours in the air, 200 bullets: Israel Aerospace Industries’ new weapons system
item.description: Israel Aerospace Industries and SIG Sauer complete a live-fire test of the FIRE STORM 250 system, which integrates an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) with an M250 machine gun, while maintaining human control over engagement decisions.

item.title: 9-month-old baby critically injured after falling from slide
item.description: A nine-month-old baby fell from a slide while playing.

item.title: Saada calls for PM indictment withdrawn, former law enforcement officials investigated
item.description: MK Moshe Saada calls for appointing a new attorney general after the elections to withdraw the indictment against Netanyahu and launch investigations alleging serious misconduct in the investigations.

item.title: Heated confrontation over UN's silence on Hamas crimes
item.description: Israeli Ambassador Danny Danon confronted UN representative Vanessa Frazier over a report on children in armed conflict that he said ignores Hamas. "But you stay silent."

item.title: France will soon call out the army to stop the barbarians
item.description: At this moment there is nothing more important in Europe, nothing more indicative of its future, than what is happening in France. Opinion.

item.title: Following security threats: Israel to ban certain types of drones
item.description: Defense Minister Israel Katz is expected to sign an order on Sunday banning the operation of fiber-optic and SIM-controlled drones for six months, following security threats.

item.title: ISIS attack plot against IDF soldiers in Jerusalem foiled
item.description: 18-year-old Umm al-Fahm resident arrested on suspicion of pledging allegiance to ISIS and planning an attack on IDF soldiers in Jerusalem’s Old City.

item.title: From Mexico to Australia: Eight Jewish educators honored at global conference in Israel
item.description: President Herzog and Minister Chikli attend inaugural Global Jewish Teacher Award ceremony, recognizing educators for contributions to Jewish identity and strengthening ties with Israel.

item.description: National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir challenges 'Together' leader Naftali Bennett to debate as they clash at Walla!, trading accusations over cooperation with Ra'am leader MK Mansour Abbas.

item.title: Jared Kushner marks one year since release of Israeli hostages: 'A moment I will never forget'
item.description:
Jared Kushner, advisor to US President Donald Trump, on Tuesday marked one year since the release of the final 20 living Israeli hostages from Gaza, recalling their reunions with their families as "one of the most special moments of my life."
"One year ago today, all 20 remaining living Israeli hostages finally came home after two years of unimaginable suffering in Gaza," Kushner wrote. "After so much pain, uncertainty, and heartbreak, seeing families embrace their loved ones again was something I will never forget." He added that the hostages "endured hell" while their families demonstrated "extraordinary strength, courage, and resilience."
Kushner expressed gratitude to President Trump for his "leadership and determination," as well as to Vice President JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and partners in Israel, Qatar, Egypt, and Turkey. He specifically thanked Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Ron Dermer, and senior officials from the countries involved for their efforts in securing the hostages' release.
"Above all, today belongs to the freed hostages and their families," Kushner concluded. "Their strength and determination will always inspire me."

item.title: Israir halts Marrakech flight sales following Flydubai attack
item.description: Israir freezes plans to expand flights to Morocco, suspends ticket sales to Marrakech following the Flydubai attack.

item.title: Yeshiva Committee issues unusual guidelines to students
item.description: Committee of Yeshivas in the Land of Israel issues unusual guidelines urging haredi yeshiva students to avoid encounters with military authorities, take precautions against legal complications.

item.title: 15-year-old girl detained for alleged racist attack on woman
item.description:
Police detained a 15-year-old girl for questioning on suspicion of assaulting a woman on a bus in Ramat Gan, cursing at her and throwing socks at her, allegedly out of a racist motive.
At the conclusion of her questioning, the girl was released under restrictive conditions.

item.title: Joint List makes Palestinian state a condition for post-election support
item.description: Yousef Jabareen says any talks on Joint List support for an alternative government must include a diplomatic path toward a Palestinian state in the 1967 borders.

item.title: Two daycare staff questioned after six toddlers escape
item.description: Police question two staff members at Petah Tikva daycare after six toddlers wandered out unsupervised, release both under restrictive conditions.

item.description: Magen David Adom teams treat approximately 10 infants suffering mild allergic reactions at Beitar Illit daycare center; all 150 infants evacuated.

item.title: Held onto munition for an hour: Disturbing details from deadly school trip explosion
item.description: Students say they found missiles and carried a cluster munition for over an hour before it exploded during lunch, killing 14-year-old Elazar Yair Wilensky.

item.title: Deadly school trip exposes confusion over unexploded ordnance
item.description: Army Radio investigation reveals conflicting claims over responsibility for clearing unexploded munitions in northern Israel, where hundreds or thousands of dangerous remnants may remain after the war.

item.title: Two employees detained after toddlers flee kindergarten
item.description:
Petah Tikva police opened an investigation following a report that several toddlers had left a kindergarten in the city and were seen wandering alone in the street without adult supervision while riding toy cars. The incident took place on Sunday.
Officers who were called to the scene located the toddlers and returned them to their parents.
As part of the investigation, two female staff members from the kindergarten, Petah Tikva residents in their 40s and 50s, were detained for questioning last night. At the conclusion of their questioning, both were released under restrictive conditions.
